label: Expects / to return an int
description: The learner expects 7 / 2 to be 3 or 10 / 2 to be int 5, not knowing / always produces a float.

remediation.explanation: / is true division and always returns a float: 10 / 2 is 5.0. Use // when you want a floored whole number.

label: Expects Python to convert between str and int automatically
description: The learner writes "5" + 5 expecting 10 or 55, or int("12a") expecting 12, as if Python coerced types for them.

remediation.explanation: Python never guesses a conversion. "5" + "5" is "55" and 5 + 5 is 10; mixing them raises TypeError, and int() refuses anything that is not a clean digit string.

label: Swaps = and ==
description: The learner uses = where a comparison is needed, writing if x = 5: and getting a SyntaxError.

remediation.explanation: A single = stores a value. A double == asks a question and answers True or False.

label: Shadows builtins like list and str
description: The learner names a variable list or str, then later calls like list(range(3)) fail with TypeError: 'list' object is not callable.

remediation.explanation: list and str are builtin types. Reusing their names replaces them for the rest of the program; pick names like items or text.

label: Forgets the colon after if, while, for, and def
description: The learner writes if score > 90 without the ending colon and hits SyntaxError.

remediation.explanation: Every block header in Python ends with a colon. The indented lines below it are the body.

label: Misjudges range and randint boundaries
description: The learner expects range(1, 4) to include 4 or randint(1, 6) to stop at 5, guessing boundaries instead of checking them.

remediation.explanation: range excludes its stop value: range(1, 4) is 1, 2, 3. randint is the opposite — both endpoints are included: randint(1, 6) can return 6.

label: Writes while loops that never end
description: The learner forgets to move the condition toward False inside the loop, so count < 3 stays True forever.

remediation.explanation: A while loop repeats as long as its condition stays True. Something in the body must change the tested variable: count = count + 1.

label: Prints instead of returning from functions
description: The learner uses print inside a function and then expects the call's value, not realising the function returns None.

remediation.explanation: print shows text on the screen; return hands a value back to the caller. No return means the call gives None.

label: Uses a mutable default argument
description: The learner writes def collect(x, items=[]) and finds state leaking between calls, because the default list is created once at definition.

remediation.explanation: Default arguments are evaluated once, when def runs. Every call that omits items shares one list; pass None and create a fresh list inside the function.

label: Indexes lists from 1 and dicts by position
description: The learner expects names[1] to be the first item, and ages[0] to return the first dict entry, treating keys as positions.

remediation.explanation: List positions start at 0: names[0] is the first item. Dicts have no positions at all — you look up by key: ages["ann"].

label: Mutates a list while iterating over it
description: The learner calls remove inside a for loop over the same list and finds items skipped, because the list shifts under the loop's cursor.

remediation.explanation: Removing while looping slides items left, and the loop's next index jumps past one. Build a new list instead: [n for n in nums if n >= 0].

label: Drops the f prefix on formatted strings
description: The learner writes "Hi {name}" without the f and prints literal braces instead of the value.

remediation.explanation: Braces only interpolate when the string has the f prefix: f"Hi {name}". Without it they are ordinary characters.

label: Opens files with w when they meant a
description: The learner opens a log with "w" and destroys its history, or thinks "r" can add content.

remediation.explanation: "w" truncates the file the moment it opens. "a" appends at the end and keeps what is there; "r" can only read.

label: Expects passing tests to print something
description: The learner runs a passing test file, sees no output, and assumes the tests did not run.

remediation.explanation: assert is a tripwire: silent when it passes, AssertionError when it fails. No output from a test run means everything passed.
